title: private-deploy-admin-hsm-region-onboarding-notes
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures UX notes, low-fi wireframe ideas, and backlog grooming items for a consolidated private deployment admin onboarding flow focused on region selection, network setup (VPC/CIDR / peering checks), and KMS/HSM integration.

Context / why this now:
- PM asks: consolidate 3 separate pages (region config, network connect, keys) into a single guided onboarding for private deployments to reduce first-time setup failures and support noise.
- Target personas: platform engineer (primary), infra SME, security architect (needs HSM/KMS auditability).
- Constraint: must map 1:1 to existing backend APIs (region catalog, network validator, kms connector) so UX should drive existing validation endpoints.

Assumptions:
- Customers may have multiple regions in different clouds; region names come from our region catalog (region id + provider + latency profile).
- KMS integrations can be one of: managed cloud KMS (AWS/GCP/Azure), customer HSM (Thales/Luna) reachable via IP & cert, or an on-prem KMS proxy.
- Network validation endpoint can test: CIDR overlap, route propagation, peering reachability, NAT gateway availability, DNS resolution to our control plane.

Goals / success metrics:
- Reduce setup time for private deployment by 40% (from metrics in PD-ONB-142).
- Decrease network-related support tickets within first 7 days by 50%.
- Provide clear audit trail and test results for KMS/HSM connector validation.

High-level Flow (single-page stepper idea):
1) Choose deployment regions (multi-select) + region affinity matrix
2) Network topology mapping (pick VPCs/subnets per region, paste CIDR or connect via cloud-connector)
3) KMS/HSM connector (add key store, set trust anchors, upload cert or select cloud provider)
4) Review & test (run network checks, key wrap/unwrap test, latency/cost estimate)
5) Provision / Save + Post-provision checklist (monitoring hooks, audit events)

Screen-by-screen details:
1) Regions screen
- Left: region list table with columns: region id, provider, availability (AZs), recommended GPU capacity, estimated monthly infra cost per unit, latency to control plane (ms).
- Right: small map + region affinity matrix showing: latency, cost multiplier, legal constraints (checkbox for data residency).
- UX notes: default preselect nearest region to customer's account location. Allow drag-to-reorder to set route priority.
- Errors: If a selected region lacks required capacity profile, show inline warning with link to request capacity.

2) Network topology mapping
- Step header: "Map your network to each selected region"
- For each region show an expandable card:
  * Fields: VPC name (free text), VPC CIDR (validate), list of subnets (with role column: inference, control-plane, mgmt), gateway (IGW/NAT) selectors, peering ID (optional).
  * Buttons: "Run network checks" (on card) and "Show traceroute" (opens modal with simplified output).
- Validation feedback: show granular checks with green/yellow/red icons: CIDR overlap, routing table (has route to our egress IPs), NAT present for outbound to control plane, DNS resolution for control-plane endpoints.
- UX edge: allow paste of whole cloud-provider VPC export JSON (AWS DescribeVpcs) into a textarea; we'll parse and prefill fields.

3) KMS / HSM connector
- Three modes with radio selectors: Cloud-KMS | Bring-your-own-HSM (BYOHSM) | Import key material
- For Cloud-KMS: dropdown for provider + IAM role ARN / service account email + test connection button.
- For BYOHSM: fields for HSM IP(s), management port, cert upload (PEM), trust anchor name, key slot id. Also optional MGF/algorithm hints.
- Key import modal: allow one-time key import (PEM/raw) with explicit checkboxes for "key origin: external" and "private key persisted by Redwood? (no/yes)". Default is "never persisted" unless enterprise license. 
- Critical UX: display allowed operations badge (wrap/unwrap, sign, decrypt) and KMS key policy snippet (read-only) so security reviewers can copy.
- Validation: run wrap/unwrap test using ephemeral nonce and show success/failure with timestamps and request ids for audit.

4) Review & test
- Compact summary: regions + network cards + key stores listed. Each row has a status dot showing last test status and timestamp.
- Actions: re-run all checks, show full logs (downloadable .zip), open individual test detail.
- Cost/latency estimate: quick panel estimating expected per-token cost delta by region selection and network egress.
- Final CTA: "Provision and Start" with small checkbox "I confirm my org policy allows storing KMS credentials in Redwood" (link to security page).

5) Post-provision checklist (in console)
- Auto-create quick links: Observability (console -> routes), audit log exporter (S3/GCS), canary policy skeleton, rollback route.

Low-fi wireframe sketches (pasteable text for sync):
- Stepper header: [Regions] -> [Network] -> [KMS/HSM] -> [Review]
- Region card example:
  +--------------------------------------------+
  | eu-west-1 | AWS | GPUs: V100/4 | latency: 22ms |
  | [select] [info] [reorder handle]                |
  +--------------------------------------------+

- Network card example (expanded):
  +---------------------------------------------------------+
  | Region: eu-west-1        [Run checks] [Traceroute]       |
  | VPC name: [redwood-vpc]  CIDR: [10.10.0.0/16] (ok)      |
  | Subnets:                                              |
  |  - inference: 10.10.1.0/24 (ok)                       |
  |  - control:   10.10.2.0/24 (warning: no NAT) [help]    |
  +---------------------------------------------------------+

Field-level validation and error states:
- CIDR: reject malformed, warn on overlapping local ranges, block if range too small for requested instance count.
- Peering: if peering ID present but our control-plane cannot reach, show reproducible troubleshooting steps and CLI cURL snippet to run from customer's bastion.
- HSM cert: parse PEM on upload and show details (subject, issuer, expiration). If cert chain incomplete, show "missing CA chain" guidance.
- KMS test failures: provide deterministic next steps: check IAM role, check network policy, check port whitelist on HSM. Include example firewall rules.

Accessibility / UX details:
- All status icons must include text labels for screen readers and tooltips.
- Keyboard-first flows for stepper and network card accordion.
- Provide a "text only" mode of the review page that is basically a JSON & test log dump for auditors.

Backlog grooming items (priority ordered):
- (P0) Network validator: return traceroute + route table snapshot (PD-360).
- (P0) KMS wrap/unwrap test API + request-id logging (PD-362).
- (P1) Paste cloud VPC export auto-fill parser (PD-345).
- (P1) Region affinity matrix UI component (reusable) (PD-376).
- (P2) Key import audit checkbox + retention guardrails (legal review) (PD-389).
- (P3) Onboarding analytics event schema for steps and failure reasons (PD-401).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we allow storing HSM credentials in our vault for reconnect/retry? (security + legal input required)
- For BYOHSM mode, do we support only public IP or private link (VPC peering) — impacts network troubleshooting flow.
- Should the review step auto-schedule a post-provision canary deploy, or leave that to the user?

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Stepper with region select, network per-region cards, KMS connector with wrap/unwrap test, review page with pass/fail statuses.
- Tests return logs with request ids and timestamps and are downloadable.
- Basic accessibility labels present.

Next steps / owners:
- UX: Arielle to mock high-fidelity screens for Region and KMS screens (due 2024-09-10).
- Eng: Diego to spec network validator output format (PD-360) and provide sample JSON for paste parser (due 2024-09-06).
- Security: Priya to advise on credential storage policy and draft guidance copy for the review checkbox (due 2024-09-12).

Notes to reviewer:
- This doc intentionally mixes technical fields and UX patterns: focus feedback on missing validation states, what tests customers will want to see for KMS, and whether the single-stepper approach is acceptable for enterprise reviewers who prefer separate pages.

TODOs (quick list):
- [ ] Add sample log output from network validator
- [ ] Add example HSM cert parsing output
- [ ] Create copy for "why we ask for these fields" micro-help text

End of doc.
